_note: Town pages (/<town>-ma, /<town>-nh) and state hubs. Facts only: county, ZIP codes, villages/neighborhoods, nearby covered towns, and a short local note. Edit here; the build generates the pages.

ma.name: Massachusetts
ma.region: the North Shore and Merrimack Valley

nh.name: New Hampshire
nh.region: southern New Hampshire and the Seacoast

towns.name: Georgetown
towns.note: Georgetown is where CasperB2B was founded. Most local customers here search by town name plus the service ("plumber Georgetown MA"), so a page and listing for each service you offer in town matters more than broad regional ads.

towns.name: Haverhill
towns.note: Haverhill is one of the largest cities in Essex County and sits on the New Hampshire line, so customers search across both states. Naming Bradford and Ward Hill on your site and listings helps you show up for searches in those neighborhoods.

towns.name: Newburyport
towns.note: Newburyport's downtown draws visitors as well as residents, so up-to-date hours, photos and reviews decide which shop or restaurant gets the walk-in. Seasonal hours belong on your Google listing and site, not just your door.

towns.name: Newbury
towns.note: Newbury spans Byfield, Old Town and part of Plum Island, and many people search by the village name rather than "Newbury". Use all three names on your pages so you match how locals actually search.

towns.name: Amesbury
towns.note: Amesbury borders New Hampshire, so service businesses here often work both sides of the line. A clear list of the towns you serve — in both states — on your site helps Google match you to those searches.

towns.name: Salisbury
towns.note: Salisbury Beach makes summer the busy season for many local businesses. Seasonal hours, current photos and fast replies to messages matter most when visitors are deciding on the spot.

towns.name: Rowley
towns.note: Rowley is a small town on Route 1 between Newbury and Ipswich, so local businesses usually serve the surrounding towns too. Listing every town you cover is how a Rowley business gets found beyond its own ZIP code.

towns.name: Ipswich
towns.note: Ipswich draws summer visitors to its beaches and restaurants on top of a year-round local customer base. Reviews and accurate hours do much of the selling for visitors who have never heard of you.

towns.name: Boxford
towns.note: Boxford is mostly residential with no big commercial strip, so many Boxford businesses are home-based or service-area businesses. A strong website and Google listing do the job a storefront would.

towns.name: Groveland
towns.note: Groveland sits on the Merrimack River between Haverhill and Georgetown, and local trades usually cover the whole area. Pages for each town you serve help you win jobs beyond Groveland itself.

towns.name: Topsfield
towns.note: Topsfield is home to the Topsfield Fair each fall, which brings a burst of visitors to town. Outside fair season, local businesses rely on residents and neighbors finding them on Google.

towns.name: North Andover
towns.note: North Andover is a busy, competitive market next to Andover and Lawrence. Specific service pages and steady reviews are what separate a local business from regional competitors on Google.

towns.name: Andover
towns.note: Andover has a dense mix of professional firms and home services competing for the same searches. Naming Ballardvale, Shawsheen Village and downtown on your site helps you rank for neighborhood searches.

towns.name: Methuen
towns.note: Methuen borders Salem, NH, and many customers compare businesses across the state line. A clear service-area list and fast follow-up help you win the comparison.

towns.name: Danvers
towns.note: Danvers sits on the Route 1 and Route 114 retail corridors with heavy competition for the same customers. Specific pages, reviews and quick replies to every inquiry are what win here.

towns.name: Peabody
towns.note: Peabody has a large retail and service economy, so local businesses compete with regional chains for search results. Reviews and complete Google listings help a local business stand out against bigger ad budgets.

towns.name: Beverly
towns.note: Beverly runs from a busy downtown to Beverly Farms and Prides Crossing, and people search by those names. Use them on your pages and listings to match local searches.

towns.name: Salem
towns.note: Salem's tourism peaks every October, when visitors search on their phones for places to eat, shop and stay. Accurate hours, fresh photos and fast replies decide who gets that traffic.

towns.name: Salem
towns.note: Salem, NH draws Massachusetts shoppers across the line, so local businesses compete for customers from both states. A service-area list covering both sides of the border helps Google show you to them.

towns.name: Nashua
towns.note: Nashua is one of New Hampshire's two largest cities and CasperB2B's mailing address is here. It's a competitive market where specific service pages and steady reviews make the difference.

towns.name: Manchester
towns.note: Manchester is New Hampshire's largest city, with the most local competition for every common search. Businesses that answer leads fastest and show the most recent reviews win the click.

towns.name: Bedford
towns.note: Bedford borders Manchester, so local businesses compete with the whole Manchester market. Naming Bedford clearly on your site and listings keeps you in front of customers searching right in town.

towns.name: Portsmouth
towns.note: Portsmouth's downtown and Seacoast attract visitors year-round, alongside a strong local business community. Reviews, photos and accurate hours do much of the selling before anyone walks in.

towns.name: Concord
towns.note: Concord is New Hampshire's state capital, with many professional and government-adjacent firms. Clear, specific service pages help those firms get found by the right clients.

towns.name: Derry
towns.note: Derry's local trades and shops serve a wide area along Route 28 and I-93. Listing the towns you cover is how a Derry business gets found beyond its own ZIP code.

towns.name: Londonderry
towns.note: Londonderry sits on I-93 between Manchester and the Massachusetts line, so businesses here often serve customers in both directions. A clear service-area list helps Google match you to those searches.

towns.name: Hudson
towns.note: Hudson borders Nashua, so local businesses compete with the whole Nashua market for the same searches. Naming Hudson clearly on your pages keeps you visible to customers searching in town.
